---
title: Tools across your app
description: "Put app-wide tools in one catalog the provider registers, then choose the pages each one is on with match, and which ones an agent may use with availableTools. No router setup."
sidebar:
  label: 4. Tools across your app
---

A tool in a component is on while that component is on the page. A tool for the **whole app** (read the cart, list
orders, go to a page) lives in one object, the **catalog**, written with `defineWebTool`. You hand it to the provider
once, and each tool's **`match`** chooses the pages it is on.

The common tools at the top come ready-made ([Common tools](/build/common-tools), next). `getCart`, `listOrders` and
`trackOrder` are yours, one file each. An object means a tool cannot be listed twice, two tools with one id fail at
startup naming both keys, and everything else refers to a tool by reference: `tools.getCart.invoke()`,
`availableTools={[tools.getCart]}`, `defineWebAgent({ tools: [tools.getCart] })`.

## `match`: on while the path fits

A catalog tool with no `match` is on everywhere. With `match`, it is on while the URL's path fits: one pattern, several,
or a regular expression.

<View title="Vite">

<include meta='title="src/tools/track-order.ts" {16-17}'>/_examples/shared/tools/track-order.ts</include>

</View>

<View title="Next.js">

<include meta='title="tools/track-order.ts" {16-17}'>/_examples/shared/tools/track-order.ts</include>

</View>

<View title="TanStack Start">

<include meta='title="src/tools/track-order.ts" {16-17}'>/_examples/shared/tools/track-order.ts</include>

</View>

<View title="Astro">

<include meta='title="src/tools/track-order.ts" {16-17}'>/_examples/shared/tools/track-order.ts</include>

</View>

```ts
match: "/orders" // one path
match: ["/orders", "/orders/:id"] // any of these
match: /^\/orders\/\d+(\/tracking)?$/ // a RegExp, tested against the path
```

A pattern is literal segments, `:param` for exactly one segment, and a trailing `*` for the rest: `/orders`,
`/product/:slug`, `/flights/*`. It is the URL the visitor sees, in every framework: Next.js's
`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` is `"/product/:slug"`. With a hash router, `#/orders` counts as the path `/orders`.

**No router wiring.** The library follows the browser's URL itself, so the provider needs nothing from React Router,
TanStack Router, Next.js or Astro. A tool turns on and off as the visitor navigates, client-side or by a full page
load. A tool that turns off in the middle of a call finishes that call first.

:::warning[A `match` tool turns on as soon as the URL changes]
That is before the new page has rendered. Do not write a `match` tool that reads state the page sets when it mounts:
read the URL, or a store that is set before the navigation. Skyline's results tools read the search, so its
`search_flights` stores the search first and navigates second. URL changes are also seen just after the navigation
call returns (Next.js changes the URL inside a React effect), so a tool turns on a moment after `router.push`, not
during it.
:::

## The three scopes

| Scope | How | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Everywhere** | A catalog tool with no `match` | `get_cart`, `get_time` |
| **Per path** | A catalog tool with `match` | `list_orders` on `/orders` |
| **Per component** | `useWebTool`, on while the component is mounted (`{ enabled }` to switch it by state) | `add_to_cart` on a product's page |

A tool in a component rarely needs `match`: it is on while the component is. `useWebTool` ignores `match`.

## Only some of them: `availableTools`

`tools` is everything the app has. `availableTools` is what an agent may use right now, decided by your own state;
left out, it is all of them. It filters the catalog, not the tools components own.

```tsx
<WebAgentsProvider
  tools={tools}
  availableTools={
    user
      ? [tools.getCart, tools.listOrders, tools.trackOrder]
      : [tools.getCart]
  }
>
```

Catalog files use `defineWebTool` from `@webmcp-agents/core`, the same function `@webmcp-agents/react` re-exports: an
agent lists catalog tools by reference, and your `/api/chat` route imports the agent on the server
([Add the chat](/build/add-the-chat)), so a file it reaches imports no React.

## Try it

Open `/orders` and, in the browser console:

```js
await agent.invoke("list_orders", { limit: 1 });
```

It answers with the newest order. Go back to `/`: in the devtools panel, `list_orders` and `track_order` are listed
**off here**, and the same call rejects because the tool is not on.

## Options you'll use most

| Where | Option | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `defineWebTool` | `match` | The paths a catalog tool is on: a pattern, several, or a RegExp. Default: everywhere. |
| `<WebAgentsProvider>` | `tools` | The catalog: every app-wide tool, by name. |
| `<WebAgentsProvider>` | `availableTools` | The tools an agent may use now, by reference. Default: all of them. |
| `useWebTool` | `enabled` (second argument) | Switch a component's tool by state. |

Every option: [`defineWebTool`](/reference/core/define-web-tool), [`<WebAgentsProvider>`](/reference/react/web-agents-provider)
and [`matchPath`](/reference/core/match-path) for the pattern syntax.
